milestone: funnel:triage — the pending queue becomes a set of batches
problem: the only adoption signal this project recognises is a human decision, and there has never been one. The queue sat at 99 pending across months. '99 pending' is a single number with no handle on it: a person opening the panel sees a wall, closes it, and the number grows.
what_it_does: groups pending artifacts by the project they came from, orders the groups by size, and shows the oldest few paths in each. One command: npm run funnel:triage (or --json).

first_run_finding.reading: 47 of the 99 — nearly half — come from one unrelated project whose artifacts are 56 days old. Clearing that single batch halving the queue is the difference between starting and not starting.

design_refusal.reason: the script is read-only and has no --approve. A CLI that marked items in bulk would not optimise this metric, it would end it — the number would move while adoption stayed at zero, and the only honest signal this project has would be gone.
design_refusal.stated_in_output: every run prints that it changes nothing and that a decision is recorded only when a person makes one in the panel

what_it_does_not_do: it does not decide which artifact is acceptable, does not read the artifacts, and does not recommend approve or reject. The grouping only answers 'which batch first'.
next_step_for_operator: run the triage, open the panel on batch 1, and read the artifacts. The first recorded decision is the first real adoption data point this project will have.
